outline.description: Presents the problem of mathematical reasoning in LLMs, the performance gap between open and closed models, and the goals and key contributions of DeepSeekMath.
subtopics: Why mathematical reasoning is challenging for LLMs
Performance landscape: open-source vs closed-source models
DeepSeekMath goals: open, strong, efficient math reasoner
Headline results: MATH 51.7% (single), 60.9% (self-consistency@64)
Key ideas: large-scale math pre-training + GRPO reinforcement learning
Contributions overview: scalable data pipeline, GRPO, unified RL paradigm, empirical analyses

outline.description: Equips readers with foundational concepts needed to understand the paper, including prompting paradigms, benchmarks, and evaluation protocols.
subtopics: Prompting for reasoning: chain-of-thought (CoT) and program-of-thought (PoT)
Tool-integrated reasoning and Python execution (e.g., sympy, math)
Formal mathematics and autoformalization (Isabelle, Sledgehammer, miniF2F)
Benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, MGSM-zh, Gaokao-MathQA/Cloze, MMLU-STEM, BBH, SAT (OCW), HumanEval, MBPP
Evaluation practices: few-shot CoT, PoT execution accuracy, self-consistency, Pass@K vs Maj@K
Data contamination risks and decontamination principles

outline.chapter_title: Building the DeepSeekMath Corpus from Common Crawl
outline.description: Explains the iterative, scalable data engineering pipeline that extracts high-quality math content from the web.
subtopics: Seed corpus and classifier bootstrapping: starting from OpenWebMath
fastText classifier setup: positives/negatives, hyperparameters, n-grams
Common Crawl preprocessing: URL deduplication and near-duplication
Scoring and top-k selection: token budgets and iterative expansion
Domain-level mining and human annotation to diversify positives
Multilingual coverage (English, Chinese, others) and its motivation
Stopping criteria and dataset scale: 35.5M pages, 120B tokens

outline.description: Details how benchmark leakage is mitigated and how data quality is validated prior to full pre-training.
subtopics: N-gram exact matching strategy for benchmark decontamination
Targets for filtering: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, AGIEval and related sets
Trade-offs in strict decontamination vs recall
Pilot pre-training for quality validation
Ethical and reproducibility considerations in web-scale data curation

outline.chapter_title: Corpus Quality Validation: Comparisons and Scaling
outline.description: Compares the DeepSeekMath Corpus against MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2 using a controlled 1.3B-parameter testbed.
subtopics: Controlled training setup: optimizer, LR schedule, batch size, context length
Learning curves and data repetition effects
Findings: higher quality, larger scale, better multilingual support
Insights from early vs late-stage performance and plateauing
Implications for corpus design and multi-epoch training

outline.description: Describes the base model initialization, training mixture, and hyperparameters that lead to strong math and general reasoning abilities.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B: why start from a code model
Training mixture: DeepSeekMath corpus, AlgebraicStack, arXiv, GitHub code, general CC (EN+ZH)
Training details: token budget (500B), batch size, learning rate
Maintaining coding capability while improving math
Cross-domain generalization to MMLU and BBH

outline.description: Summarizes comprehensive evaluations across natural language math reasoning, tool-assisted solving, formal math, and general understanding/coding.
subtopics: CoT performance: GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, MGSM-zh, MMLU-STEM, Gaokao-MathQA/Cloze
PoT performance with Python tools (math, sympy)
Formal theorem proving: informal-to-formal with Isabelle and Sledgehammer on miniF2F
General capabilities: MMLU, BBH, HumanEval, MBPP
Self-consistency sampling and its effects on accuracy
Key observations vs open-source/closed-source baselines (e.g., Minerva 540B)

outline.chapter_title: Supervised Fine-Tuning for Mathematical Instruction Following
outline.description: Covers the construction of the 776K-example SFT dataset and the training of DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B for both CoT and tool-integrated reasoning.
subtopics: English datasets: GSM8K, MATH (with tool-integrated solutions), MathInstruct subsets, Lila-OOD
Chinese datasets: K-12 coverage across 76 subtopics with CoT and tool-integrated formats
Formatting and concatenation, context length, batch, learning rate
Performance without tools and with tools vs open and closed models
Observations on capability gains and remaining gaps (e.g., vs GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra)

outline.chapter_title: Reinforcement Learning Foundations: From PPO to GRPO
outline.description: Introduces GRPO, a PPO variant that removes the critic by using group relative baselines, improving memory efficiency and training stability.
subtopics: PPO recap: actor-critic, value function, GAE, per-token KL penalty
Limitations in LLM fine-tuning: memory cost of critic, sparse end-of-sequence rewards
GRPO design: sampling groups per question and using group average as baseline
Objective structure: clipping, KL regularization against reference policy
Practical memory/computation benefits and training stability considerations

outline.chapter_title: GRPO in Practice: Outcome Supervision, Process Supervision, and Iterative RL
outline.description: Explains how rewards are computed and normalized in GRPO, and how iterative training continuously improves both policy and reward models.
subtopics: Outcome supervision: single reward at end of output, group normalization (mean/std)
Process supervision: step-level rewards, cumulative advantages, fine-grained signals
KL divergence estimation and hyperparameters (beta, epsilon)
Group size and sampling strategy (e.g., G=64) and its effects
Iterative RL loop: replay buffer, reference model update, reward model continual training
Engineering tips: batching, context length, update frequency

outline.description: Details the GRPO training of DeepSeekMath-RL 7B and its performance gains on in-domain and out-of-domain tasks.
subtopics: RL data: CoT-format subsets of GSM8K and MATH from SFT (~144K questions)
Reward model training and initialization (from DeepSeekMath-Base 7B)
Policy training hyperparameters: LR, KL coefficient, batch sizes, max length
In-domain gains: GSM8K and MATH; out-of-domain gains: CMATH and others
Comparison to SFT-only model and other 7B–70B baselines
Interpretation of improvements and sample efficiency

outline.chapter_title: Ablations and Empirical Insights on Pre-training Data
outline.description: Presents controlled studies on the effects of code training and arXiv data in math reasoning performance.
subtopics: Code training hypotheses and experimental designs: two-stage vs one-stage
Effects on PoT (tool use) and CoT (no tool) capabilities
Catastrophic forgetting and mixing strategies for code+math
ArXiv-only training results: lack of gains or deterioration across tasks
Caveats and open questions about arXiv data utility and scaling

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm for SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO
outline.description: Provides a common mathematical view to understand these methods via data source, reward function, and algorithmic gradient coefficients.
subtopics: General gradient formulation: data source, reward function, algorithmic GC
Method mapping: SFT, RFT, DPO, Online RFT, PPO, GRPO
Online vs offline sampling: advantages of online data in later stages
Gradient coefficients: differential reinforcement in GRPO vs uniform RFT
Outcome vs process supervision: step-aware coefficients and performance
Why RL appears to work: improving Maj@K over Pass@K (distribution robustness vs fundamental capability)

outline.chapter_title: Practical Guidance: Reproducing and Extending DeepSeekMath
outline.description: Offers actionable steps and best practices for building similar systems, from data engineering to evaluation.
subtopics: Replicating the data pipeline: CC processing, classifier training, domain mining
Decontamination workflow and audits
Pre-training stack: frameworks (e.g., HAI-LLM), optimizers, schedules, context lengths
SFT recipe: dataset formats, batching, LR, multilingual considerations
RL setup: group sampling, reward model building, iterative training
Evaluation protocols: CoT, PoT, formal math, self-consistency
Compute, memory, and cost considerations

outline.description: Discusses current weaknesses (e.g., geometry), alignment issues, and research directions in data, algorithms, and reward modeling.
subtopics: Observed limitations: geometry, theorem proving gaps vs closed models
Few-shot limitations and model scale effects
Data source expansions: higher-quality web mining, better coverage of geometry
Advanced sampling/decoding for RL and efficient inference
Robust RL under noisy rewards: weak-to-strong alignment
Reward model generalization and uncertainty estimation
Building scalable process reward models
Ethical considerations in web-scale data usage and multilingual biases

outline.description: Summarizes the DeepSeekMath approach and its implications for open mathematical reasoning models.
subtopics: Large-scale, high-quality web math data unlocks strong reasoning in smaller models
Code-first initialization benefits mathematical reasoning
GRPO: efficient, effective RL without a critic, with outcome/process supervision and iterative training
Unified paradigm clarifies relations among popular fine-tuning and RL methods
Outlook: building more general, robust, and efficient math reasoners in the open
